validity.recommendation: Hold as under-sourced / possible phantom. Do not treat 48in/350 MMcf/d as corroborated. Seek independent corroboration (SOMO/Ministry of Oil, North/South Gas Co, Iraqi press) for a real, named 48-inch eastern dry-gas trunk before keeping as a standalone 'operating' row; otherwise merge into the north-south dry-gas trunk rows or reclassify.
validity.researcher_notes: The GEM row rests on a SINGLE citation: Dr. Jafar Dhia Jafar / Uruk Engineering, 'The Power & Gas Challenge for Iraq', Iraq Energy Forum, 29 March 2018 (iraqenergy.org PDF). I extracted the PDF text (pdftotext): slide 8 is titled 'Iraq's Existing Dry Gas Pipeline Connects North & South' and its map labels 'Taji-Duara Gas Pipeline', 'Eastern Gas Pipe Line / 48 Inch, 350 mmscfd', and 'AL Mansuriya'. So the source DOES name the line (GEM renamed 'Eastern Gas Pipe Line' -> 'Eastern Iraq Gas Pipeline') and presents it as an EXISTING dry-gas trunk on the eastern side of the country -- this is not pure fabrication. BUT the support is weak on every axis: (1) it is one non-independent presentation slide, not two independent sources; (2) the specifics (48 in, 350 mmscfd) come only from that map annotation, with no length, no endpoints, no start year, no operator on the source; (3) scripts/url_verifier.py returns 200 but CANNOT confirm the PDF's distinctive text tokens ('Eastern Gas Pipe Line', '48 Inch', '350 mmscfd', 'Dry Gas Pipeline') because the PDF content streams are compressed -- only the fluke token 'gas' matches, so the sheet's own cited value is not machine-verifiable. (4) Independent web + Arabic-context searches for a 48-inch eastern dry-gas trunk (Mansuriya/Diyala/Taji north-south) surfaced NOTHING naming this pipeline -- only Mansuriya-field development news. A 48-inch trunk would be the LARGEST-diameter gas line in the whole Iraq roster (every other trunk is <=42 in: P4061 National 42in, P1852/P2234 Trans-Iraq 42in), which makes an undocumented 48-inch line more suspicious, not less. Net: real-ish per one 2018 slide but unverifiable and uncorroborated -> existence concern.

If it is the eastern branch of that trunk it should be a named segment, not a standalone generic 'Eastern Iraq' row.
validity.researcher_notes: The sole source frames this line as part of 'Iraq's Existing Dry Gas Pipeline Connects North & South' -- exactly the physical system GEM already represents via P4061 (National Gas Pipeline -> Basra), P1852 (Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha), and the Trans-Iraq segment family (P4062/P4064/P4065/P4066). The slide shows the Eastern line as DISTINCT from Taji-Duara (P4054, 18in), so it is NOT a Taji-Duara duplicate, and its 48in differs from the 42in trunk rows, so this is a relabel/segment-double-count RISK rather than a proven duplicate. Cannot confirm identity without endpoints (row has start=end=Iraq). Flagging so a human can reconcile against the trunk rows rather than carrying a generically-named 48-inch 'Eastern' line separately.

validity.recommendation: If retained, classification as a gas transmission line is defensible; do NOT reclassify to oil.
validity.researcher_notes: The one source explicitly calls it a DRY GAS pipeline ('Iraq's Existing Dry Gas Pipeline Connects North & South'), i.e. a gas transmission trunk, not a gathering/process/feeder line and not one of the GulfPub Iraq crude/NGL lines (none of those is a 48in gas line; GulfPub has no Iraq gas coverage). So Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are consistent with the source. Classification is the one axis that holds up -- the problem is existence/corroboration and possible duplication, not commodity misclassification.
